task: Compare user satisfaction across 4 tourism domains (accommodation, indoor attractions, outdoor attractions, destination) via harmonized 1-5 scale + robust Z, per-source stats, and one-way ANOVA.

methods.harmonization: All four raw variables were already on a 1-5 integer/float scale, so only range verification (min>=1, max<=5) and NaN removal were needed - no linear rescaling. Sources: Airbnb_Open_Data.csv['review rate number'] (accommodation), indoors.csv['rating'] (indoor_attraction), outdoors.csv['rate'] (outdoor_attraction), tx_clean.csv['Rating'] coerced with pd.to_numeric(errors='coerce') (destination, derived from TripAdvisor Transaction.xlsx).
methods.robust_z: Within each source independently: z=(x-median)/(1.4826*MAD), MAD=median(|x-median|). No source hit the MAD==0 fallback.
methods.source_statistics: Per source on robust-Z scores: n, mean, sample std (ddof=1), se=std/sqrt(n), 95% CI = mean +/- t_{0.975,n-1}*se (scipy.stats.t.ppf).
methods.anova: scipy.stats.f_oneway on the four robust-Z vectors; eta^2 = SS_between/SS_total with SS_between=sum(n_g*(mean_g-grand_mean)^2); companion omega^2 = (SS_b - df_b*MS_w)/(SS_t + MS_w).
methods.diagnostics: Pairwise Welch t-tests with Cohen's d (pooled by df) on all 6 pairs; Brown-Forsythe/Levene (median-centred) on raw 1-5 values; venue-level sensitivity ANOVA aggregating FISETIO months to one value per mus_ID (n=27) / park_id (n=83); raw 1-5 ANOVA for reference; log10(p) computed via chi2(3) tail asymptotics because p underflows in float64.

levene_raw_1to5.note: variance heterogeneity is severe; equal-variance F-test is only approximate

key_findings: Ordering on robust-Z (deviation from own median in robust SD units): accommodation +0.188 > destination +0.106 > outdoor_attraction -0.189 > indoor_attraction -0.650.
One-way ANOVA: F=1064.888, df=(3, 160798), p<1e-300 (log10 p ~ -692), eta^2=0.0195 -> statistically decisive but SMALL effect (Cohen: 0.01 small, 0.06 medium).
All 6 pairwise Welch contrasts are significant at alpha=0.05; p-values are driven by the large N (~1.6e5) rather than by large gaps.

Robust-Z comparison measures how far each domain's central tendency sits from ITS OWN median, not absolute satisfaction; on the raw 1-5 scale the ranking is different (outdoor 4.67 > indoor 4.38 > destination 4.16 > accommodation 3.28) and eta^2 rises to 0.127.

Caveat: FISETIO rows are venue-month aggregates (pseudo-replication). Aggregating to venue level (27 museums, 83 parks) keeps significance (F=128.0, p=8.6e-83) but eta^2 drops to 0.0025, so the between-domain differences, while real, are of modest magnitude and dominated by the accommodation (Airbnb) distribution.
Levene on raw values is highly significant (statistic 4764.6, p~0), confirming unequal variances; robust scaling and Welch post-hoc were used accordingly.

output_schema.output1.csv: source, n, mean, std, ci_lower, ci_upper (on robust-Z scores)
output_schema.output2.csv: statistic, p_value, effect_size (one row: one-way ANOVA)
